Khata Khatauni No.273, Khasra No.529, situated at Mohal Sawindhar, Tehsil Karsog, District Mandi
and to pay him compensation in accordance with law.

The adjoining land parcels co-owned by these two persons were
also utilized by the respondents for construction of the same road, i.e. Mahota-Bagshar road,
without acquiring the land.
No compensation was paid to these persons.

The aforementioned
persons instituted Civil Writ Petitions, bearing Cwp No.2386 of 2009 (Bhoop Ram Versus State of

sentences.text:
Cwp No.2386 of 2009 was allowed on 24.06.2016 with
following operative directions:-
"(a) The respondent-State shall initiate the steps to acquire the land of the petitioner
which has been utilized for the purpose of construction of Mauta-Bagshar Road
within a period of three months from today.
(b) In case the respondent did not intend to acquire the land of the petitioner, then
the respondent may re-align the road by "bye passing" the property of the petitioner
within a period of three months from today and vacate the land of the petitioner.

In the eventuality of the respondent-State deciding to vacate the land of the petitioner, which has
been used by it for the purpose of construction of road in issue, then the respondent No.1 shall have
the damage caused to the land of the petitioner assessed from the Pwd and revenue authorities of
the State of Himachal Pradesh and pay to the petitioner the amount of .
compensation so assessed with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of writ petition.

In
case the petitioner is not satisfied with the valuation of compensation/damage assessed by the
authorities concerned, then he shall be at liberty to approach the appropriate Forum/Court of law
for the redressal of his grievance in this regard, i.e. enhancement of compensation/damages."

Cwp No.3090 of 2009 was allowed on 05.07.2016 with following directions:-
"(i) Respondents are directed to initiate process for acquisition of the land of
petitioner utilized for construction of road in accordance with law within 3 months
from today and complete entire process within a period of one year thereafter.

(ii) Respondents may avoid acquisition of the land of petitioner either by vacating his
land by constructing road from alternative route without utilizing land of the
petitioner or adopting any other mode for restoring his land.

In such eventuality
respondents-State shall have to pay compensation, duly assessed from experts, to
petitioner for utilization of his land till vacation.

(iii) Needless to say that on dissatisfaction with valuation of compensation of
damages assessed by the authorities concerned, petitioner may avail remedy
available to him for enhancement of compensation/damages in accordance with law."
2(iii). The respondents have implemented the decisions in the aforesaid two cases.

The award was
passed in the aforesaid two cases in complian
ce to the decisions dated 24.06.2016 and 05.07.2016 on 22.02.2022

. The land owned by S/Sh. Bhoop Ram & Neem Chand utilized by the 4 2024:HHC:6918-DB respondents for construction of the road in question has since been acquired and they have been duly compensated in terms of the award.

The petitioner also moved representation to the .
respondents on 08.04.2022 seeking compensation in lieu of his land utilized by the respondents for the construction of the same very road.

The Land Acquisition Collector vide his communication dated 21.04.2022, directed the Executive Engineer, HPPWD Division Karsog, District Mandi to take appropriate action in the matter in accordance with law.

It is the grievance of the petitioner that no concrete steps have been taken till date by the respondents for acquiring his land even though the land has been utilized by the respondents for the purpose of construction of the road in question.

With that grievance, this writ petition has been filed seeking following substantive reliefs:-
"i) Issue a writ of Mandamus or other appropriate writ or direction, directing the respondents to acquire the land of the Petitioner on Khasra No.529 situated at Mohal Sawindhar, Tehsil Karsog, District Mandi, H.P. (utilized for the construction of Mahota-Bagshar Road) and pay compensation in accordance with law i.e. The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, in a time bound manner.

3 3(i).

Mahota-Bagshar road with total length Km 0/00 to 17/00 upto Village Telehan was constructed under .
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojna (in short 'PMGSY') under a package for the year 2003-04.
The road from Km 7/780 to 14/00 was constructed by the respondents prior to 2/2009.

Petitioner's land falls at RDs between Km 8/240 to 8/300 and Km 8/435 to 8/486.
3(ii).
The aforesaid land of the petitioner was duly utilized for the construction of the road in question.
The said utilization was based upon the verbal consent of the petitioner.
The cutting work of the road through the land in question was completed before 17.01.2005.
The petitioner never objected at the time of construction of the road, therefore, the land of the petitioner cannot be acquired.
Compensation cannot be paid to the petitioner.
3(iii).
Under the PMGSY, there is no provision for acquisition of the land on payment of compensation.
Petitioner's claim suffers from delay and laches.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterated the pleadings in the writ petition and also placed reliance upon the judgments passed in the cases of co-owners of the 6 2024:HHC:6918-DB adjoining land parcels, i.e. Sh. Bhoop Singh1 and Sh. Neem Chand2.

Reliance was also placed upon a judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Full Bench in State of Himachal Pradesh and others Versus Sita Ram Sharma 3 in .
support of the claim made by the petitioner for acquisition of his land utilized by the respondents for the construction of the road in question and to pay him compensation accordingly.

sentences.text: Learned Additional Advocate General opposed the petition primarily on the grounds that the claim of the petitioner suffers from delay and laches.

The road was constructed in the year 2005, whereas,
the petitioner had claimed the relief of acquisition of his land for the first time by preferring representation to the respondents on 08.04.2022.
It was also submitted that there is no provision under the PMGSY for acquisition of the land.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
In my considered view, the petitioner has made out a case in his favour.

This is for the following reasons:-
5(i).
The respondents have not disputed that the subject land owned by the petitioner had been utilized by them for construction of Mahota-Bagshar road.

sentences.text: 4 The respondents have also not disputed that the land parcels owned by S/Sh. Bhoop Ram and Neem Chand, which were adjoining to the subject land, had also been utilized for the construction of the same road.

It is a matter .
of record that the writ petitions instituted by S/Sh. Bhoop Ram and Neem Chand were allowed on 24.06.2016 and 05.07.2016, directing the respondents to initiate the process for acquisition of the lands of the petitioners (therein) for construction of the road in accordance with law.

It is also a matter of record that the respondents have since implemented the aforesaid decisions and in terms of award No.5/2022, dated 22.02.2022, acquired the lands owned by S/Sh. Bhoop Ram and Neem Chand.
Compensation as per the award has been paid to the aforesaid persons.
The petitioner is sailing in the same boat.
In the given facts of the case, it is not open for the respondents to discriminate the petitioner.

Once the land of some of the land owners utilized for construction of the road in question has been acquired by the respondents, it is incumbent upon them to give same treatment to the present petitioner, whose land was also utilized for construction of that very road.
5(iii).

It would also be appropriate to refer to the judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court on 8 2024:HHC:6918-DB 28.06.2023 in CWP No.6581/2021 (Labdhu Ram Vs. State of H.P.
& Ors).

The petitioner therein had raised a factual plea that though certain others, whose lands were utilized for the road, were paid the compensation, but he .
was denied the same even though his land was also utilized for construction of same road.
Road in that case was laid in the year 1995-96.

Taking note of various pronouncements, viz. (1986) 2 SCC 68 (State of Himachal Pradesh Vs Umeed Ram Sharma); (2016) 7 SCC 498 (Swaraj Abhiyan(I) vs.
Union of India and ors.); (2020) 9 SCC 356 (Hari Krishna Mandir Trust vs. State of Maharashtra &
Ors.); (2020) 4 SCC 572 (D.B. Basnett Vs. Collector East District, Gangtok, Sikkim and Anr.);
(2021) 14 SCC 703 (B.K. Ravichandra and Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors.); (2022) 7 SCC 508 (Sukh Dutt Ratra & Anr. Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors.), the contention of delay and laches raised by the respondents-State was turned down.

sentences.text: The observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court that the State cannot evade its legal responsibility towards those from whom private property has been expropriated, were reiterated.

It will be appropriate to extract following paragraphs from Labdhu Ram's case (supra):-
9 2024:HHC:6918-DB "18.
In Sukh Dutt Ratra, supra, the appellant's land had been utilized for construction of road in 1972-73 without initiating any proceedings for acquisition and without paying any compensation.

When the petitioner filed a writ petition on the basis of relief granted to other owners whose land was so acquired,
the said Writ petition was dismissed by the High Court holding that .
there were disputed questions of law and fact for determination on the starting point of limitation,
which cannot be adjudicated in the writ proceeding and the petitioners were given liberty to approach the Civil Court.

Decided On: 13Th August vs State Of H.P. And Others on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199804575/
5

entities.text: 13Th August vs State Of H.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Supreme Court reversed the said decision and held that nobody can be deprived of liberty or property without due process, or authorization of law and the State has a higher responsibility in demonstrating that it has acted within the confines of legality, and had not tarnished the basic principle of the rule of law.
It held that State, merely on the ground of delay and laches, cannot evade its legal responsibility towards those from whom private property has been expropriated.

It observed that the State was initiating acquisition proceedings selectively and not in every case like that of the appellants whose land was taken, and at every stage it sought to shirk its responsibility of acquiring land required for public use in the manner prescribed by law.
It held that the State cannot shield itself behind the ground of delay and laches in such a situation as there cannot be a limitation to doing justice.
It also rejected the plea alleged verbal consent or lack of objection on the ground that no material was placed on record to substantiate the said plea and held that the State was unable to produce any evidence indicating that the land of the appellant had been taken over or acquired in the manner known to law, or that it had ever paid any compensation.
It declared that there is no period of limitation prescribed for the courts to exercise their constitutional jurisdiction to do substantial justice.
It directed the State to treat the subject land as a deemed acquisition and disburse compensation to the appellants therein in terms of similar orders passed in other cases within four months.

19. In view of the above settled legal position, we are of the opinion that the stand of the State that it need not 10 2024:HHC:6918-DB pay any compensation for utilizing the petitioner's land for the purpose of laying a road cannot be countenanced and the State is bound to pay market value compensation to the petitioner for utilizing his land for the purpose of the road.

20. Therefore, the writ petition is allowed with costs of Rs.10,000/- and a direction is issued to the .
respondents

to demarcate the land of the petitioner utilized for the purpose of the road in question within four weeks, treat it as having been acquired for the said purpose and pay him the highest amount towards compensation among compensation under the awards Annexures P-3 and P-4 with all statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act,1894 within eight weeks."

The question as to "whether a person whose land has been utilized for construction of road under 'PMGSY' is entitled to compensation" came up for consideration before the Hon'ble Full Bench in State of Himachal Pradesh and others Versus Sita Ram Sharma3 alongwith connected matter.

entities.text: State of Himachal Pradesh and others Versus Sita Ram Sharma3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Vide decision dated 30.03.2022, the question was answered in affirmative that a person whose land had been utilized for construction of road under PMGSY is entitled to compensation unless it is proved to the satisfaction of the Court that the land was voluntarily donated or given by him willingly with free will and consent for construction of such road.

Decided On: 13Th August vs State Of H.P. And Others on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199804575/
6

entities.text: 13Th August vs State Of H.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the respondents have not established that the land was voluntarily donated or given by the petitioner willingly for construction of the road in question.

The decision rendered by the Hon'ble Full Bench 11 2024:HHC:6918-DB in Sita Ram Sharma's case effectively answers the contention raised by the learned Additional Advocate General that compensation cannot be directed to be paid in case of construction of road under PMGSY.
.
In view of above-referred decisions, the relief prayed for by the petitioner cannot be declined on the basis of plea of delay and laches.
The respondent, being a welfare State, has to act in just and fair manner after following the due process of law.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case and in light of the legal position, this writ petition is allowed.

The respondents are directed to initiate the process for acquiring subject land of the petitioner utilized for construction of the road in accordance with law within a period of eight weeks from today and complete the entire process within a period of one year thereafter.
The writ petition stands disposed of in the above terms, so also the pending miscellaneous application(s), if any.
